newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai govt fully backs economic policies - Amnuay.
newsitem.headline: Thai govt fully backs economic policies - Amnuay.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan on Tuesday reiterated that he enjoyed the full backing of the ruling coalition government and its agencies on his policies to address current national economic problems.

Amnuay told reporters on return from a roadshow to publicise Thailand's $500 million yankee bond issue in Hong Kong that a local newspaper report speculating he may resign in protest at conflicts over his economic policies was erroneous.
He had made a similar denial on Monday.

"My work has received good cooperation, both in monetary and fiscal policies, from ministers and coalition leaders during tabling of motions in parliament and parliamentary debates. I have never confided with any subordinates (about reported plan to resign)," Amnuay said.

He added that Moody's Investors Service was the sole international rating agency reviewing a possible downgrade of Thailand's long-term sovereign debts while others still voiced confidence in its economy.
S&P, the other major rating service, said last week it had confidence in the Thai economy.
"Every agency has confidence in us and the only exception has not managed to get market response (to its review on Thailand)," he said.
"I have met Moody's regional representative who is a son of my friend. I briefed him on Thai economic fundamentals," the minister said.

Amnuay said he briefed foreign investors on Thailand's still robust economy and convinced them that its measures to curb inflation and the wide current account deficit were adequate and on the right track.
He said the baht's return to stability this week, which dealers said was due to dollar softness and the absence of attacks by speculators, reflected sustained foreign confidence in Thailand.
